notes: §1985:IV.4.3.8.2.3 SR7 (added by Amendment 1): "The subscript ALL may be used only when the subscripted identifier is used as a function argument and may not be used when condition-name-1 is specified." ALL is read in one place, TryBindAllArgument: a function argument that is a sole data reference whose subscript list holds ALL binds as one table operand the backend enumerates, on a function whose format repeats an argument (RepeatsAnArgument, the condition of §1985:p.A-28: "When the definition of a function permits an argument to be repeated a variable number of times"; COBOL1645 otherwise), and the name must be a data item (FindReportedItem refuses a condition-name, COBOL1639). Every other subscript list goes through InterpretSubscripts, where ALL is no arithmetic expression and MaterializePosition refuses it with COBOL2363 (IllegalPositionMessage). The one place a later edition also admits ALL, the rightmost subscript of a table SORT (§2023:8.4.2.3.3 SR6, the admitRightmostAll arm of InterpretSubscripts), is unreachable at 85: VisitSortStatement refuses the table SORT with COBOL0870. Probed at --std 85: SUM, MAX, MIN, ORD-MAX, ORD-MIN, MEAN, MEDIAN, RANGE, MIDRANGE, VARIANCE and PRESENT-VALUE take E (ALL), a qualified table, (ALL ALL), (2 ALL), (ALL 3), (IX ALL), an OCCURS DEPENDING table (the range is the object's value) and two ALL arguments in one list, each with the right value and the rightmost ALL varying first; ALL is refused in MOVE (both sides), DISPLAY, ADD, IF, PERFORM TIMES, STRING, INITIALIZE, CALL USING, SEARCH and SORT, on a condition-name in IF, SET and as a function argument, in SQRT, MOD, INTEGER and LENGTH, inside an expression argument (E (ALL) + 1, a parenthesized or negated one), as a subscript of a subscript, with a reference modifier, and with the wrong count of subscripts. The witness computes FUNCTION SUM (E1 (ALL)) and then writes MOVE E1 (ALL) TO W1, refused with COBOL2363.

next.reason: §1985:IV.4.3.8.2.3 SR7 (added by Amendment 1, X3.23a-1989; Errata C92): "The subscript ALL may be used only when the subscripted identifier is used as a function argument and may not be used when condition-name-1 is specified." 2023 splits it in two and adds a case. §2023:8.4.2.3.3 SR6: "The subscript ALL may be used only: — When the subscripted identifier is used as an intrinsic function argument, or — as the rightmost or only subscript of a table in the table format of a SORT statement." §2023:8.4.2.3.3 SR7: "ALL shall not be specified if qualified-condition-name-1 is specified." The words that differ: "or — as the rightmost or only subscript of a table in the table format of a SORT statement", a use of ALL that 1985 refuses and 2023 accepts (a lifted restriction). The function-argument case and the condition-name prohibition are the same.
